perception_loop.assessment: Three framed renders were used. The agent inspected the whole board early, inspected the dense rollout region after building it, then made multiple targeted additions and routing/label corrections before a final whole-board QA render. This forms two render→adjust→render intervals. Close-up use was somewhat sparse for a 131-call, multi-region build, but the dense rollout region received a framed look and the final render reported clean diagnostics.

lint_etiquette.assessment: All lint errors and warnings were resolved before commit. Sixteen newly reported E-class lint findings appeared across the build, primarily edge-label coverage and routing conflicts. The agent changed routes, anchors, label positions, wording, or edge representation rather than repeatedly issuing an unchanged operation. The articles-label sequence was a short skirmish, but the strategy changed on each turn and did not meet the rubric's lint-fight definition. No warning was committed or overridden, so no commit-summary override reason was required.

commit_honesty.assessment: The sole commit summary accurately describes the stage diff. The diff contains guarded input/output flow, per-call vault credentials and action integrations, durable-profile extraction and cold-history archival, champion/challenger sampling, automated judging, product-owner approval and rejection, rollback retention, and independent regression removal. The final render was diagnostically clean, and no seen defect was left undeclared.

economy.assessment: The committed patch contains 63 operations, proportionate to a complex four-region architecture diagram. The session completed in approximately 14.81 minutes, narrowly within the 15-minute budget, and finalized well below the 300-turn limit. There was one localized add–reroute–delete cycle for the rollback edge, but it was a prompt consolidation in response to an anti-parallel-edge lint rather than broad destructive thrashing.
